where these numbers come from
  • realThe opening frame: the saved count checker (share-0.0 U-Net, trained on the 10 pairs among digits 0 to 4, job 94108) run layer by layer on the canvases apart_1_3, wrong_1_3, apart_3_4 and wrong_3_4 at t = 712, 616, 539 and 480 by explain_stages.py (job 94116). Its layer-by-layer logit had to match the head's own to 1e-4 or the job would stop; it did not stop. Feature maps are stored as float16.
  • realThe noise frame's curves: the saved count checker's balanced accuracy at each of the 16 timesteps, on digits 5 to 9 it never saw (0.791 over all 16) and on digits 0 to 4 (0.782), from ../numbers/real/count-final.json (job 94108, W&B tyhrpyov).
  • illustrativeThe miniature: every weight, the frozen expert (ε∅ = 0.9x; asking for digit y subtracts 0.5·Ty·σ(3x)), the noise draw on the four pixels (0.5, −0.3, 0.2, −0.6), and the training step of 0.05 on a batch of two.
  • realThe 16 timesteps and their ᾱ (linear betas, canvas_unet.py lines 35 to 38; v2_learn.py line 46), the time features (checker.py lines 69 to 73; the miniature keeps the first frequency's two), the two canvases apart_1_3 and wrong_1_3 (data hash f70b0fb3…), every layer shape and weight count, and the training counts.
  • The noise on the real canvases is one numpy draw (seed 0) shared across all 16 levels. The checker draws its own.
  • Scores: count 0.774 on pairs holding 4 and 0.781 on trained pairs (job 94085's log lines); identity 0.555 and 0.603 (the V2 review, 05-does-it-learn/review.md); one combined checker 0.704 on all kinds and 0.511 on apart against wrong (job 94080).
  • Every number is read from page_key.json, written by make_page_key.py, which reuses ../2-miniature/miniature.py. At t = 480 its 94 values equal that miniature's own key. Its hand gradients match central differences to 2.6e-09, and this page checks them again live.
what is not drawn
  • The frozen U-Net's inside. It has skip connections; here it is one grey box, and the miniature stands in a formula for it.
  • Skip connections in the checker: PixelHead has none, so none are drawn.
  • The three stem convolutions and c1 become one convolution with one window per half; c2 is left out; the MLP's hidden layer of 256 and its SiLU are left out; 16 time features become 2.
  • Adam at 0.001 on 256 canvases for 4,000 updates becomes one plain step of 0.05 on two canvases.
  • Count's other three kinds of canvas (overlaid, same half, single).
  • The identity checker's real maps, logits and gradients: it was never saved, so every identity number on this page is the miniature's and stays illustrative.
  • In the opening frame, all but 8 channels of each layer. The 8 shown are the ones with the largest mean value on that canvas at that timestep; a different canvas or timestep can pick different ones.
  • The weights on the miniature's lines: they show on hover or tap, and in the panel's tables, so the figure keeps room for the values.
  • The push in the miniature uses its starting weights, not trained ones.
how to read the page
  • Blue: pixels and time. Green: trained units. Red: the logit. Orange: anything flowing backward. Grey: frozen. Purple: count. Teal: identity.
  • A circle holds the value at that node. Hover or tap a line to read its weight; the panel lists them all.
  • In the opening frame's real pictures, blue is below 0, white is 0 and red is above, and each picture saturates at the 99th percentile of its absolute values, so one hot pixel cannot wash out the rest. Canvases are grey from −1 (black) to +1 (white).
  • The right arrow key or next moves one idea on. In the opening frame, step or a click on a stage moves the red box. Play replays the current pass, step moves it one layer, and sweep noise runs the 16 timesteps.
